follow-on: the baseline arm is mislabeled and does not match the shipped test. baseline-cross-ids.log records revision=a1ae3fd536e7d23b851d0f5e6d08c91b43739a1d with no working-tree marker, but tests/ids/test_mappable_ids_from_candidates.py does not exist at a1ae3fd (git show a1ae3fd:tests/ids/test_mappable_ids_from_candidates.py reports 'does not exist in a1ae3fd'), so the arm ran base production code against a test added by 1f996327 while reading as a clean-base run. Its failing test test_selected_and_escalated_candidate_homes_extend_default_ids is also a different test than the shipped test_selected_candidate_home_extends_default_ids the negative control exercised, so the test-first defect evidence and the shipped guard are not the same test. The manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite also run different commands (the focused file versus the full gate), so their direct difference is not a like-for-like added-failure count.

follow-on: the candidate-home union is applied only inside branch C (no domains and no ids_filter), so an IDS holding a selected or escalated candidate edge but no domain overlap is still excluded when --domain or --ids is given, and is skipped entirely by the early return at tools.py:423 when no enriched source carries a physics_domain. The plan's wording ('an IDS holding a selected or escalated candidate edge for the facility is a target even when the domain overlap misses it') is unqualified; the current placement satisfies the default-enumeration case and the node's tests, but the filtered paths do not get the same union.

justifications.durability: the guard fires and I reproduced it independently: removing the union loop from tools.py makes tests/ids/test_mappable_ids_from_candidates.py::test_selected_candidate_home_extends_default_ids fail, EXIT=1, which is the reviewed run's own negative control reproduced. The two tests/cli/test_discover_sequence.py additions (callback.assert_called_once and the nothing-to-do skip) pin the mapping stage's default engagement and its empty-route skip, so a regression in either reddens.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced both arms and the negative control independently in scratch trees of the reviewed revision (source under /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261008T082444866521-review-of-sequence-mapping-stages/arms and .../arms-base, PYTHONPATH at the scratch tree, module.__file__ confirmed at /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261008T082444866521-review-of-sequence-mapping-stages/arms/imas_codex/ids/tools.py for the head and .../arms-base/imas_codex/ids/tools.py for the base): head 1f996327 ran the full gate to '558 passed, 5 skipped, 3 deselected' EXIT=0, matching the reviewed run's committed-gate.log; the head focused test ran to '1 passed' EXIT=0 and head with the union loop removed ran it to '1 failed' EXIT=1. The base arm (tools.py at a1ae3fd, focused test) ran to '1 failed' EXIT=1, confirming the recorded defect reproduces. The shortfalls are in the reviewed run's own record: baseline-cross-ids.log labels itself revision=a1ae3fd with no working-tree marker although the test file it ran does not exist at a1ae3fd (the reviewed commit adds it), its failing test test_selected_and_escalated_candidate_homes_extend_default_ids differs from the shipped test test_selected_candidate_home_extends_default_ids whose guard the negative control exercised, and the baseline and head arms run different commands.
justifications.fit: the added symbols are named by mechanism (no plan labels, section numbers or ticket ids); the union loop reuses the branch-A/B query idiom and the shared dd_clause; the branch-C comment was corrected to describe source domains and candidate homes, and the new test file name names the behaviour, not the plan.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the three done-when behaviours are present and pinned: the candidate-home union is in tools.py and its test proves a cross-domain home survives the default enumeration; the mapping stage's single pipeline call and its nothing-to-do skip are pinned by the two tests/cli/test_discover_sequence.py additions. The shortfall is that the plan names a node fragment among its write paths and it was not produced, so the node's evidence lives only in the manifest.
justifications.reuse: the union reuses the existing GraphClient query pattern, the _dd_version_clause helper and the ids_by_name accumulator rather than a parallel enumerator; the two test additions reuse the existing test_discover_sequence.py fixtures (healthy, _stage, _config) and the map_run monkeypatch seam sequence-runner established, adding no new helper.
justifications.scope_discipline: the commit touches only the declared imas_codex/ids/tools.py and tests/cli/test_discover_sequence.py plus the declared new tests/ids/test_mappable_ids_from_candidates.py - no production file beyond tools.py, no pyproject or lock change, no unrelated edit. sequence.py was correctly left unmodified because the mapping-default and nothing-to-do behaviours predate this node. Declaring the node fragment and figures dir and then not producing them is an evidence shortfall rather than scope creep.
